Approval is requested to assign the operation and maintenance of dewatering discharge
treatment at the Marina Asset to M/s Al Saad General Contracting Company, the current
Marina Basin contractor, for the period from July 2024 to December 2024. Upon
approval, the Commercial team will process a Variation Order to formalize this scope of
work.

At present, Al Saad, through its sub-contractor M/s ACTION, is responsible for dewatering
discharge treatment under the TB-Marina Basin Contract, which technically concluded on
June 19, 2024. However, a 103-day extension is being processed, with the revised contract
completion date expected to be September 30, 2024. Additionally, Al Saad has been
awarded the contract for the Fixed Jetty, extending its presence on the Marina Asset site
until February 2025.

A comparison of quotations between Al Saad and Action International Services LLC was
conducted. While Action International offered lower operational costs, their proposal
includes additional expenses for environmental surveys and higher demobilization costs,
which make Al Saad’s offer more competitive overall.

Based on the commercial assessment, approval is sought to award the contract to Al
Saad for continued dewatering discharge treatment from July 2024 to December 2024

Name *: PVO 017 -Amaala Marina Navigation MBES Survey.
Description:
This scope involves the commissioning of an independent Multibeam Echo Sounder (MBES) survey for the Amaala Marina to validate the Contractor’s as-built Bathymetric Survey and confirm compliance with the marina’s
navigational requirements.
The new work package for navigation simulation has been awarded to the consultant “M/s Royal Haskoning.” Recently. The consultant has stated that they require an independent multibeam bathymetric survey of the entire marina basin,
including the entrance channel, in accordance with their specifications.
The marine survey was already part of MME’s original scope of work; however, due to the revision in specifications and the increase in the area to be surveyed, there will be an additional cost impact, with no impact on time.
Following a technical review by Haskoning, it was concluded that the existing bathymetric datasets contain inconsistencies and cannot be relied upon for Navigation Simulation and Hydrodynamic Modelling. For a marina targeting the
Superyacht (80m+) and Megayacht (100m+) sector, such data ambiguity presents a significant operational, safety, and liability risk.
The independent MBES survey is required for the following reasons:
1.Squat and Under-Keel Clearance (Safety Critical)
Superyachts navigating confined channels experience “squat,” which is highly sensitive to water depth. A variation of 0.3m–0.5m may determine the difference between safe transit and grounding within simulation models. A definitive seabed
baseline compliant with IHO S-44 Special Order standards is therefore required for navigation sign-off.
2.Wave Transformation and Basin Tranquility (Design Critical)
Hydrodynamic and wave models rely on accurate seabed geometry to predict wave refraction and shoaling as waves approach the marina. Inaccurate bathymetry would compromise basin tranquility assessments and Real-Time Simulation
outputs.
3.Liability and Insurance
Navigational simulations act as the project’s Digital Twin for safety validation, pilot training, and channel approval. Use of uncertain data would result in qualified reports, potentially impacting insurance underwriting and Captain approvals.
Although a 65m superyacht has successfully maneuvered within the marina under ideal weather and occupancy conditions, this does not validate safe operations under adverse weather, varying occupancy levels, or confined vessel interaction.
Accordingly, commissioning an independent high-resolution MBES survey is considered a safety-critical requirement to eliminate data discrepancies and ensure operational, regulatory, and insurance compliance.

due to tight project schedules and permitting deadlines.
